page: Amazon Web Services m6in.32xlarge is a general purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C). Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine provisions 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 64 physical cores with two threads per core running at 3.5 GHz. It includes a 54 MB L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI. The host provides 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local instance storage is attached, requiring all persistent and non-volatile data to rely on network-attached block storage over a baseline 200 Gbps network interface.

Benchmark results highlight significant multi-core throughput and network capability. The instance demonstrates top-tier computational capabilities with a PassMark CPU score of 86,880.06, supported by high scores in PassMark CPU extended instructions (106,624.39) and cryptographic encryption (111,587.3). In multi-threaded evaluation, stress-ng CPU achieved 123,857.55 and Geekbench multi-core hit 16,116.0, placing it in the upper quartile. While single-thread workloads perform moderately in the median band—yielding a 1,891.8 single-core stress-ng score and 1,698.0 in Geekbench single-core—parallel processing metrics such as Clang compilation (51,288.0) and ray tracing (95,806.0) perform strongly.

Data manipulation and network-heavy testing reveal robust transactional metrics, including Redis SET throughput reaching 107.77 million operations per second and static web serving throughput hitting 69.71 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 334.39 GB/sec alongside 135.57 GB/sec write bandwidth. Small model (135M) prompt processing registers at 2,796.03 tokens per second, but generation speeds scale downward on larger parameter counts (2.8 tokens per second for 70B generation) due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

The instance serves as a high-throughput platform for enterprise applications with high networking demands. Cost efficiency derives from high compute and memory capacity paired with 200 Gbps bandwidth, though omitting bundled local NVMe storage requires planning for separate network storage. It is suitable for large-scale distributed databases, in-memory caching systems, CI/CD compilation farms, and high-concurrency web serving infrastructure.
description: Amazon Web Services m6in.32xlarge is an Intel-based general purpose instance managed by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs (64 physical cores at 3.5 GHz) via Intel Xeon 8375C processors, 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 200 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no local storage or GPUs, directing all disk I/O to network-attached storage. Benchmark data places the instance in top tiers for multi-core compute, cryptographic operations, and ray tracing, with strong results in Redis caching operations and static web serving, alongside steady middle-tier single-threaded marks. The instance provides high data density and throughput for enterprise workloads, large relational databases, in-memory caches, distributed microservices, and intensive multi-threaded compilation pipelines.
